column3: The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name at the end; BSB says Him.
The Hebrew pictures consideration as setting the heart on Job and ruin as swallowing him up.
The Hebrew uses bless euphemistically for curse; it names bone and flesh in that order, where BSB reverses them.
The Hebrew says hand in the singular; BSB says hands.
The Hebrew describes striking him with a bad boil and names the sole of his foot in the singular; BSB says infected and soles of his feet.
The Hebrew leaves Job unnamed here, using pronouns; BSB names him.
The Hebrew uses bless euphemistically where BSB says curse.
The Hebrew names his lips; BSB says what he said. Only is not explicitly stated before good.
The Hebrew says they did not recognize him; BSB says they could barely recognize him.
